deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics. It is administrative and personal material written on the back of a sheet of theta-function computations (the previous and next pages deal with theta functions). There are three items.

(1) A draft receipt. Riemann confirms that the Dean, Hofrath Professor Waitz (the historian Georg Waitz, then Dean of the Göttingen Philosophical Faculty), paid him his share of the doctoral promotion fees for 28 candidates. The names are Ulmann, Buff, Menge, Stegemann, Stevens, Tockenckner(?), Lorey, Cooper, Bithall(?), Davies, Rösler, Penchmann(?), Hunyady(?), Aronstein, Stille, Berlien(?), Credner, Caspari, Strüver, Kühner, Kaiser, Popp, Pierse(?), Hassemüller(?), Toleers(?), Wibel, Moldenhauer and Wehohake(?). The fee is 6 Thaler each, giving 28 × 6 = 168 Thaler. The first line of names is struck out and rewritten, and the Dean's title is corrected to 'Herrn Hofrath'.

(2) A second receipt. It covers Riemann's share of the 'Quarta (Quaestur?) inscriptionum', the matriculation-fee share, for Winter Semester 1863/64. The amount is 34 Thaler, paid through Dean Waitz. It is signed 'B. Riemann' and dated 'Pisa'.

(3) A draft letter from Pisa to a Göttingen confidant addressed as 'Du'. The page does not establish who this is; possibly someone handling his affairs in Göttingen.
- Riemann writes that he feels depressed at not having written for so long, because of his poor health.
- He had hoped to send a finished piece of work to Göttingen, and had some weeks when his condition was not worrying, but then it worsened again.
- Unfavourable weather combined with digestive trouble harmed his chest: he once coughed up blood and avoided worse only through extreme caution.
- So he can now send only the requested receipts.
- He does not know whether he will be granted further leave.
- A 'Professorin Schulz' wrote to Elise (his wife) that a Hanover newspaper reported he would stay in Italy.
- He suspects that the position (presumably the Pisa chair offered him via Betti in 1863) would only have been offered if he had declared himself fit to lecture last summer. How things now stand, he does not know.

The only computation on the page is 28 · 6 = 168. It is correct, and the list indeed contains 28 names.

results.what: Fee arithmetic: 28 candidates at 6 Thaler each = 168 Thaler
Biographical record: Riemann in Pisa in winter 1863/64, haemoptysis, uncertainty about further leave from Göttingen, and allusion to a position (Pisa chair) offered to him
results.usually_credited_to: Known in outline from Dedekind's biography of Riemann (1876) and later biographies (Laugwitz)

deep.surprise_reason: There is no mathematical content: only fee receipts and a personal letter draft. Riemann's illness and stay in Pisa in 1863/64 and the Pisa chair offer are well documented. The page has minor archival value only, for example as a list of Göttingen doctoral candidates around 1863/64 and for dating the adjacent theta-function sheets to Riemann's Italian period.

checkable.asserts: 28 promotions at 6 Thaler each give 168 Thaler
the list of names contains exactly 28 candidates, consistent with '28 à 6 Thlr'

transcription_corrections: 'Quaestur inscriptionum' is probably 'Quarta inscriptionum' (the image suggests 'Quarte/Quarta'), i.e. the professor's quarter-share of matriculation fees.
'Toleers' is plausibly 'Tollens' (Bernhard Tollens, chemistry doctorate at Göttingen 1864); uncertain.
Several other names ('Tockenckner', 'Bithall', 'Penchmann', 'Pierse', 'Hassemüller', 'Wehohake') are uncertain readings and could be checked against Göttingen promotion records for 1863/64.
The first 'Pisa' (before the second receipt) is struck out in the original; the dateline 'Pisa,' heads the letter draft.
'ich war mit meiner Verdauung in Ordnung' may read 'nicht in Ordnung' given the context (digestion and weather together harmed his chest); verify against the image.
In the deletion '[-in denen auf dauerhaft ich mein-]', 'dauerhaft' may be a different word; the deleted passage is hard to read.
